signature: A dimmed roller rink that feels like the one back home: a maple oval under neon tubes and a star-shaped light, muffled pop from the DJ booth, a free arcade, a free food court and the Coach, who will not let you stay too long

exits.method: noclip into any working arcade game
exits.source_quote: No-clipping into any working game in the arcade portion will transport one to Level 40
exits.label: Pushed into a working arcade machine until it let you through
exits.hint: The machines by the arcade's rink entrance are all switched on.

exits.source_quote: a white door in this level with the number 70 engraved on it
exits.label: Opened the white door engraved 70 at the back of the arcade
exits.hint: Ask the Coach to lead you out; he knows the way to the back of the arcade.

exits.method: door labelled "Employees only!" in the food court
exits.source_quote: a door labeled "Employees only!" in the food court will send you to Level 232
exits.label: Went through the door marked "Employees only!"
exits.hint: In the food court, past the end of the counter.

entity_policy: SOURCED, DOCILE FACELINGS ONLY, never combat (class: Devoid of Harmful Entities). The Coach (striped uniform, brown hair, faceless; lessons, small talk, leads you to the white door when asked or after a long stay), the food court clerk (blank name tag; free food; silent about the Backrooms; refuses litterers), the DJ (appears and disappears in the south booth), and lone customers: one skates the oval, one plays pinball, one sits in the Cinema, one in the food court. Jonathan is a past incident (notes only). The Venosha are represented by an empty temporary camp.
content_note: The page's diary describes a wanderer's slide into apathy and his death by dehydration. Shown only in paraphrased notes; nothing graphic.
notes: SOURCE: infinitely looping rink, rink is the largest part and the usual arrival; smooth wooden floor in a loop; short wooden gate with flaps onto rough black carpet; colourful fluorescent tubes in patterns, a star-shaped fixture at the centre, mostly dimmed; muffled pop, skates on wood, laughter, pizza smell (text); DJ station on the south side with a docile Faceling sometimes picking songs; arcade east of the rink looping back to its north entrance, games free with a green card from a metal box (blue button, card catcher); Ski-Ball, big game wheels, air hockey, pinball, a few 1980s cabinets; food court (pizza, wings, foot-long hot dogs, soda fountain with almond water; Faceling with a blank name tag serves free, refuses Backrooms questions, cleans up and refuses litterers); square tables, orange plastic chairs, orange and green metal benches by the walls, condiment stand by the queue, trash cans and a taped sign by the exit; skate rental with blue walls and a US size chart, run by the Coach (free lessons, remembers names, leads you out if asked or after a prolonged stay, always welcome back); Cinema north past TV screens (large TV, three continuous metal benches stepped like stairs; leave by walking south); no permanent communities, Venosha temporary camps. TESTIMONY used: the white door 70 in a back area of the arcade with machines off or under cloth, the Coach showing it; the diary entries (paraphrased notes). ADAPTATION: the layout and all dimensions are ours (hall 56 x 32 m, maple oval 34 x 18 m, the arcade as a ring around an island of machines, the sunken back room -0.72 m, the raised DJ booth +1.08 m, the cinema floor stepping -0.9/-0.45/0 m); the infinite loop is the oval (a Faceling skates it forever), not a huge building; the comfort decay timings (fade from 2.5 to 10 min, the Coach seeks you at 5.5 min and leads you out at 12 min) are ours; skates make you faster on the maple; the star fixture turns slowly; the Coach-led exit uses the white door because the page names no destination for it (EXT#4 is not built as its own edge).
